  `k M² ≤ M + (k−1)β` has now been *solved*: `meanAgree_le_capacityCurve` gives
  `M ≤ (1 + √(1 + 4k(k−1)β))/(2k)`, the hub family sits exactly on that curve
  (`hub_on_capacityCurve`), and the curve crosses the pairwise ceiling exactly at the
  threshold — strictly below it above the threshold (`capacityCurve_lt_ceiling`),
  strictly above it below (`ceiling_lt_capacityCurve`). So the "phase transition" is
  precisely the crossing point of the two independent bounds, and each is the
  operative one on its own side. The sandwich `√β ≤ M*(k) ≤ √β + 1/k` upgrades the
  previous cycle's one-sided asymptotic into an exact limit:
  `capacityCurve_tendsto_sqrt` shows `M*(k) → √β`.
* **Closed this cycle (Conjecture 2, rigidity half).** The equality analysis
  conjectured last cycle is now a theorem, and cleanly so, because the whole
  inequality chain compresses into one *identity*
  (`saturation_defect_identity`): the slack equals the Cauchy–Schwarz defect of the
  matched-count profile plus the unused pairwise budget. Saturation therefore forces
  both defects to vanish, giving exactly the two conjectured conditions —
  constant matched count at every position (`saturation_matchCount_constant`) and
  full exhaustion of every pairwise budget together with
  `agreeSet H (Aᵢ) ∩ agreeSet H (Aⱼ) = agreeSet (Aᵢ) (Aⱼ)`
  (`saturation_pairwise_tight`), i.e. the shared model *is* the consensus and the
  fine-tunes' deviation sets are as disjoint as the budget allows.
* **New, and not conjectured last cycle.** Rigidity has an arithmetic corollary:
  extremal serving is **quantised**. `saturation_quantised` shows an extremal family
  has `M = c/k` and `β = c(c−1)/(k(k−1))` for an integer `c ≤ k`. Hence the extremal
  budgets form a finite set for each `k`; an irrational budget can never be extremal
  (`no_saturation_of_irrational_budget`), and at the measured NET-54 baseline
  `β = 0.8327` no family of twelve fine-tunes is extremal
  (`net54_no_saturating_family_of_twelve`) — the shortfall from the bound is forced by
  the arithmetic of the budget, not by slack in the proof.
* **Closed this cycle (Conjecture 2, exact converse).** Quantisation is not merely a
  necessary condition. `quantised_values_are_exactly_realised` constructs, for each
  `2 ≤ c ≤ k`, the family of all `c`-subsets of the `k` fine-tunes (positions = blocks,
  model `i` outputs a distinguished token exactly on the blocks containing `i`), and
  computes its statistics exactly by a double count of `Nat.choose`: pairwise
  agreement `c(c−1)/(k(k−1))`, mean agreement with the constant hub `c/k`, and
  saturation of `k M² = M + (k−1)β`. Since `capacityCurve_at_quantised_budget` shows
  the curve takes the value `c/k` there, the design sits exactly on the capacity curve
  (`design_on_capacityCurve`). Together with `saturation_quantised` this **classifies**
  the extremal set: attainable ⟺ quantised. The obstruction at the NET-54 budget is
  therefore genuinely arithmetic and not an artefact of the proof.
* **Failed / needed a different definition.** The first attempt to read the collapse
  as a violation of the Hamming triangle inequality is arithmetically impossible: the
  measured profile sits *inside* the budget with slack 0.7039. The right invariant
  turned out to be the *novelty* fraction. Likewise, summing pairwise triangle
  inequalities cannot see any `k`-dependence; only the second-moment (multiplicity)
  count does. And this cycle: the tempting statement "the capacity curve is always at
  least as strong as the pairwise ceiling" is **false** — it fails for every family
  below the threshold, which is why the operative bound is the minimum of the two.
* **Structural pattern.** Every result in this thread is an instance of one principle:
  agreement is a pseudometric, so identity is a *budget* that transplantation spends,
  and sharing spends it again across the served family. The bulk swap spends almost
  none of it; the tail swap spends nearly all of it; each additional fine-tune served
  from the same weights spends a further share; and the configurations that spend it
  perfectly are rigid, quantised hubs.

## Conjecture 1 — Fractional-cover formula for the general served family

Rigidity pins the *extremal* families; it does not yet evaluate a general one.
Conjecture: for an arbitrary family `A₁, …, A_k`, the best simultaneous agreement
`max_H min_i agr(H, Aᵢ)` equals `1 − ν/2`, where `ν` is the value of the fractional
cover LP of the pairwise-disagreement hypergraph (vertices = positions, one hyperedge
per disagreeing pair).
**The key insight is** that the defect identity now separates the two obstructions —
a Cauchy–Schwarz defect that measures *imbalance across positions* and a budget defect
that measures *unused pairwise room* — and the fractional cover is exactly the LP whose
optimum makes both vanish simultaneously.
**Why now?** `saturation_defect_identity` reduces the analysis to two nonnegative
quantities, and `saturation_pairwise_tight` already identifies the tight configuration
as a covering design; the remaining step is LP duality, not new combinatorics.

## Conjecture 2 — Quantisation gap: a quantitative anti-saturation bound

`saturation_quantised` says extremal budgets are the rationals `c(c−1)/(k(k−1))`.
Conjecture: the bound degrades *continuously* in the distance to that set — if
`β` is at distance `δ` from `{c(c−1)/(k(k−1)) : c ≤ k}`, then every shared model
satisfies `M ≤ capacityCurve k β − f(δ, k)` with `f(δ,k) ≍ δ/(k(1−β))`, and in
particular a family at the NET-54 budget loses a computable amount below the curve.
**The key insight is** that the two defects in the identity are themselves quantised —
the matched count is an integer, so a non-integral optimum forces a Cauchy–Schwarz
defect of at least one "quantum" `N/4`.
**Why now?** The integrality is already exposed: the proof of `saturation_quantised`
extracts the integer `c` from the constancy of `matchCount`, so the quantitative
version only needs the constancy relaxed to a near-constancy estimate. And the
qualitative converse is settled — `quantised_values_are_exactly_realised` shows every
quantised pair *is* attained by a complete `c`-design — so the only remaining content
is the rate at which the bound decays off the quantised set.

## Conjecture 3 — Dose–response linearity of the novelty floor

Swapping `k` consecutive tail layers should produce a novelty floor that grows
concavely in `k` and saturates by `k = 2`, whereas a bulk `k`-swap should keep the
floor negative for all `k` below the tail boundary.
**The key insight is** that the floor `β − min(agr(H,A), agr(H,B))` is a monotone
functional of the swap, so a dose–response curve of *floors* — not of raw agreements —
separates "entanglement depth" from "amount of perturbation".
**Why now?** The floor is a proved, computable functional
(`novelFrac_ge_baseline_sub_agree`); one- and three-layer swaps cost one experimental
arm each and immediately populate the curve.

## Conjecture 4 — Margin scarcity, not weight distance, predicts non-portability

The fraction of margin-uncertified positions in a block predicts that block's
transplant damage, and does so better than any norm-based distance between the two
copies of the block.
**The key insight is** that `net54_margin_failure_fraction` converts an agreement
measurement into a *lower bound on margin scarcity* with no free parameters, so the two
candidate predictors can be compared on the same held-out set without training
anything.
**Why now?** The catalog already contains the norm-based predictor
(`Novelty.TailSwapAttribution.output_divergence_upper`) and now the margin-based one;
a single experiment discriminates them.

## Conjecture 5 — The serving-capacity law `M(k) = (1 + √(1 + 4k(k−1)β))/(2k)` in the wild

The curve is now proved to be the exact extremal value. Conjecture: measured
multi-adapter serving degradation follows it within measurement error, and the
observed gap to the curve is itself the family's distance from hub geometry — so the
gap, not the value, is the diagnostic. At `β = 0.8327` the twelfth fine-tune is the
first that provably cannot be served at the pairwise ceiling, and no family of twelve
can even sit on the curve.
**The key insight is** that capacity is not a property of the architecture but of the
*pairwise agreement statistic* of the served family, measurable from forward passes
alone before any sharing is attempted.
**Why now?** `meanAgree_le_capacityCurve` (upper bound), `hub_on_capacityCurve`
(attainment) and `net54_no_saturating_family_of_twelve` (arithmetic obstruction) make
the prediction numerically explicit at the measured baseline.
